cohort: Pregnant women, some with and some without asymptomatic bacteriuria, were followed to observe maternal and fetal outcomes.
finding: Pregnant women with asymptomatic bacteriuria had higher rates of preterm birth (25%) and low birth weight (16.6%) in their infants compared to non-bacteriuric pregnant women, while maternal anaemia rates were similar (75% vs. 77.2%) between the groups.
